summary: FireLens: The Research Gallery is an interactive, pixel-art web experience that transforms NASA microgravity combustion research into an explorable evidence dashboard. Users navigate a virtual research facility, complete investigation quests, compare experiments, inspect measured test conditions, and trace findings back to original NASA Physical Science Informatics records. FireLens analyzes 646 retained test rows across seven investigations, including BASS, FLEX, Saffire, and SAME-R. Its VT ARC SI integration is designed to generate concise, source-cited explanations; when the external model connection is unavailable, FireLens safely falls back to ranked NASA evidence instead of producing unsupported claims. By combining an approachable game-like gallery with transparent calculations, citations, limitations, and provenance, FireLens helps students, researchers, and aerospace engineers explore complex fire-safety research relevant to future spacecraft, lunar habitats, and pressurized rovers.
details:
NASA combustion investigations span different fuels, oxygen concentrations, pressures, airflow conditions, and experimental scales. FireLens helps students, educators, and aerospace researchers find relevant evidence while keeping these important differences and limitations visible.

FireLens combines a pixel-art exploration game with a research dashboard. Visitors move through three connected gallery wings, follow SPARK’s quests, inspect exhibits, collect NASA source cards, and record findings in a device-local research journal. Keyboard, touch, click-to-walk, map, and accessible directory controls support different ways of exploring.

The Research Desk analyzes 646 retained test rows from seven NASA Physical Science Informatics investigations: BASS, BASS-II, FLEX, Saffire-I, Saffire-II, Saffire-III, and SAME-R. Users can search curated research summaries, filter tests, visualize recorded measurements, compare conditions, inspect original CSV cells, and follow DOI links to NASA sources. FireLens preserves missing, approximate, qualitative, and ambiguous values instead of silently inventing data. Original CSV files, hashes, provenance records, exclusions, and documented limitations are included.

A server-side VT ARC SI workflow retrieves a bounded evidence pack and requests concise explanations with source identifiers and limitations. Generated responses must pass citation and numeric validation. If the external model service rejects or cannot complete a hosted request, FireLens automatically displays ranked NASA evidence rather than presenting unsupported AI output. This evidence-first design is especially important because the project concerns spacecraft fire-safety research.

FireLens was developed with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Node.js, Python, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub, and the VT ARC LLM API. Automated tests check dataset counts, missing-data handling, source provenance, citation validation, FLEX calculations, API behavior, gallery navigation, collision boundaries, and quest order.

The project is creative because it turns a potentially overwhelming scientific repository into a quest-driven research gallery without treating the game as a fire simulation. It does not certify materials, predict fire risk, or provide operational safety instructions. Its intended impact is to make NASA combustion evidence easier to discover, compare, understand, and audit while supporting safer future spacecraft, lunar habitats, and pressurized rovers.
